question: Should OpenClaw add a session-key pattern allowlist mode for session tools, or fold this use case into a broader per-capability/per-agent session authorization redesign?
rationale: This changes transcript/session authorization and public config semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the durable boundary or matching rules without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fold Into Unified Session Authorization
options.body: Use the related per-capability and per-agent work to design one coherent model that can express trusted group sharing without adding a competing one-off mode.

options.title: Approve Narrow Session-Key Allowlist
options.body: Accept `tools.sessions.visibility="allowlist"` and require a focused implementation with fail-closed pattern validation across all session tools.

options.title: Keep Current Modes
options.body: Decline the new config surface for now and tell operators to use existing `agent`, `all`, A2A policy, or external workspace bridges.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Unified Session Authorization
recommendation.body: Use the related per-capability and per-agent work to design one coherent model that can express trusted group sharing without adding a competing one-off mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current session-tool security boundary points to Peter Steinberger's prior security scoping work.
